replies.author: FilipeDM
replies.body: If you already have all the assets, the AI can potentially put the game together from a single prompt. But if you want it to create all the assets from scratch as well, the whole process could take months.

replies.author: impulsivetre
replies.body: Bingo. Tons of games are made with asset packs because the assets themselves are a body of work. Building a game and telling a story is something you can do with AI as it's really just putting the pieces together. Love these results

replies.author: FilipeDM
replies.body: You can certainly create everything from scratch using Codex, provided you have the tools installed on your PC, but your credits will run out quickly, and it will take months to complete the task. Therefore, it is better to use ready-made resources to save yourself the extra work.

replies.author: BanjoThunderbird
replies.body: You won't get a good game from a single prompt even if you have preexisting assets unless it's very simple gameplay and you get lucky. It can get 80% of the way there, but the last 20% is the endless tweaking and attention to detail that has always separated good developers from bad ones.

replies.author: FilipeDM
replies.body: For a game to be good, it just needs to be fun. Some people find enjoyment in the gameplay, others in the story or the challenges, others in the graphics, and so on.

replies.author: BanjoThunderbird
replies.body: Agreed. What I'm saying is that the fine tuning required to make a game fun is challenging and AI currently does not do a good job of it.
